parsed.headline: Thousands rally in Tel Aviv, Israel, against Prime Minister Netanyahu ahead of election

pages.text: Thousands of Israelis gathered in Hostages Square in Tel Aviv on a Saturday to protest against the government of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The demonstration occurred three days before Israel’s general election, scheduled for October 20, 2026. The rally was organized by the October Council, a group founded by the families of captives taken to Gaza three years ago, to demand accountability for government failures in preventing the Hamas attack on October 7, 2023. The October Council stated on X that the event was intended to demand the establishment of a state commission of inquiry.  According to Al Jazeera, opposition figures joined the protesters, including Gadi Eisenkot of the Yashar party and Yair Golan, leader of the Democrats. Eisenkot is described as Netanyahu’s main center-right rival. Polls ahead of the October 20, 2026, election suggest a tight race between Netanyahu’s right-wing bloc, which has been in power since late 2022, and Eisenkot’s bloc, with neither currently projected to obtain a majority of seats in parliament. Haaretz reported that anti-government demonstrations were also occurring elsewhere in Israel.

parsed.headline: Awutu Senya West MP expresses confidence in NDC retaining parliamentary seat

pages.text: Gizela Tetteh-Agbotui, the Member of Parliament for Awutu Senya West in Ghana, stated she is confident the National Democratic Congress (NDC) will retain the constituency in the next general election. Her comments were made during the NDC constituency executive elections, where she dismissed concerns that the recent election of a New Patriotic Party (NPP) regional chairman from the area might improve the NPP's chances of winning the parliamentary seat. Dr. Kwabena Essibu, who is from Senya Breku within the constituency, was recently elected as the Central Regional chairman of the NPP. Tetteh-Agbotui disclosed that she personally congratulated Dr. Essibu on his election but informed him of her determination to retain the seat for the NDC. She described the constituency as an important electoral hold for her party and urged NDC members to maintain unity following the constituency executive elections. Tetteh-Agbotui called on the newly elected executives to strengthen party structures and mobilize members ahead of the next general election.

parsed.headline: Speakers call for grant-based climate finance for Bangladesh

pages.text: Speakers at a dialogue in Dhaka, Bangladesh, on October 24, 2026, urged developed nations to provide climate finance in the form of grants rather than loans. During the “National Position Paper Unveiling and Dialogue” organized by ActionAid, participants called for climate justice, increased access to the Loss and Damage Fund, and the strengthening of youth-led climate initiatives ahead of the 31st UN Climate Change Conference (COP31), scheduled for November 9-20. Speakers noted that while Bangladesh contributes less than 0.5 percent of global carbon emissions, it remains among the countries most vulnerable to climate change. Shama Obaed Islam, the State Minister for Foreign Affairs, stated that funding is required to address the loss of life and suffering in coastal, rural, and urban areas, but emphasized that such funding must be provided as grants instead of loans. Islam added that at COP31, Bangladesh intends to highlight the disproportionate impacts of climate change on the health and sanitation needs of women and children. Additionally, Islam noted that Bangladesh aims to generate 20 percent of its electricity from renewable sources by 2030 and 30 percent by 2040. SM Munjurul Hannan Khan, executive director of Nature Conservation Management, stated that developing countries have submitted climate plans but are awaiting technology transfer, capacity-building support, and adequate funding from historically responsible nations. Prof Ahmad Kamruzzaman Majumder, a director at the Center for Atmospheric Pollution Studies, called for direct funding for city corporations, methane monitoring infrastructure, waste prevention measures, and grant-based municipal financing to address climate housing needs.

parsed.headline: Ghana Health Service announces closure of type 2 poliovirus outbreak

pages.text: The Ghana Health Service (GHS) announced the successful closure of a type 2 poliovirus outbreak in Ghana in August 2026. In a statement issued on Saturday to commemorate World Polio Day 2026, the GHS said the milestone was confirmed through Outbreak Response Assessments (OBRA) and followed sustained immunisation campaigns, strengthened disease surveillance, and coordinated outbreak response measures. The GHS stated the achievement was made in collaboration with the Ministry of Health and international partners, including the World Health Organization (WHO), UNICEF, Gavi, Rotary International, and the United States Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). Ghana joins Burundi, Guinea-Bissau, the Republic of Congo, and Uganda, which also closed their type 2 poliovirus outbreaks in August 2026.

The GHS attributed the progress to years of investment in routine immunisation, supplementary vaccination campaigns, and community mobilisation. The Service disclosed that since introducing the Inactivated Polio Vaccine (IPV) in 2018 and adding a second dose in 2024, Ghana has consistently maintained immunisation coverage above 95 per cent. Despite the closure, the GHS cautioned against complacency, stating that continued surveillance and vaccination remain essential to preventing new outbreaks. This year's World Polio Day is being observed under the theme “One Day, One Focus: Ending Polio for Good,” highlighting the importance of community participation and ensuring eligible children receive necessary vaccines.

parsed.headline: Syria condemns armed attack on church in Jordan

pages.text: The Syrian Foreign Ministry issued a statement on Friday condemning an armed attack targeting St. George’s Church in the Karak governorate of southern Jordan. According to a report from the North Press Agency, the attack inside the church killed seven people and wounded several others. 1. In its official statement, the Syrian Foreign Ministry expressed solidarity with Jordan, stating that the country stands with the kingdom’s leadership and people against threats to its security, stability, and national fabric. 2. The ministry categorically rejected all forms of terrorism targeting civilian security. 3. The statement extended condolences to Jordan’s leadership, its people, and the families of the deceased, while wishing a speedy recovery to those wounded.

parsed.headline: Transit riders and advocates claim Durham Region candidates are overlooking public transit needs

pages.text: As the municipal election approaches in Durham Region, Canada, some transit riders and advocacy groups say local candidates are treating public transit as a background issue. These groups warn that the transit system is struggling to keep pace with community needs. The Durham regional council, which consists of elected mayors and regional councillors, is responsible for decisions regarding Durham Region Transit. Michael Gemmink, a rider from Pickering, expressed the view that candidates have failed to address these responsibilities throughout the election cycle.

parsed.headline: Two killed and at least 15 injured in bus-truck collision in Brahmanbaria, Bangladesh

pages.text: Two passengers were killed and at least 15 others were injured following a head-on collision between a passenger bus and a sand-laden truck in the Sarail upazila of Brahmanbaria, Bangladesh. According to Abdul Halim, officer-in-charge of Khatihata Highway Police Station, the accident occurred in the Berotola area of the Dhaka-Sylhet highway on a Saturday morning. The collision involved a Diganta Paribahan bus, which had departed Rangpur for Sylhet on Friday night, and a sand-laden truck traveling from the opposite direction. The impact left the bus overturned on the road. The deceased were identified as 32-year-old Sourav of Parbatipur upazila, Dinajpur, and 18-year-old Asif of Rangpur Sadar upazila. Police and local residents rescued the injured and transported them to Brahmanbaria Sadar Hospital. While most received primary treatment, three individuals were later sent to Dhaka in critical condition. Officer-in-charge Halim stated that legal action regarding the accident is underway.
